div.head: I Cn 18.2
div.ab: ⁊ ure ælc oðrum beode þæt we willon, þæt man us beode: þæt is rihtlic dóm ⁊ Gode swiðe gecweme; ⁊ se byð swiðe gesælig, þe þone dom gehylt.
And ælc ure oðrum beode þæt we wyllan, þæt man us beode: þ[æt] is rihtlic dom ⁊ Gode swyþe gecweme; ⁊ se byð swiðe sælig, þe þonne dom gehealt.
⁊ ure ælc oðrum beode þæt we wyllan, þæt man us beode: þæt is rihtlic dóm ⁊ Gode swiðe gecwéme; ⁊ se bið swiðe gesæli, ðe ðæne dóm gehealt.

Et quod nobis fieri uolumus, aliis faciamus: hoc iudicium iustum est; et sane beatus et Deo gratus est, qui iudicium hoc sincere tenuerit ad gloriam omnipotentis Dei, cuius sumus miseratione conditi et pretio magno redempti.
⁊ ure ælc oðrum beode þæt we wyllan þæt man us beode; þæt is rihtlic dóm ⁊ Gode swiðe gecwéme; ⁊ se bið swiðe gesæli ðe ðæne dóm gehealt.
And each of us shall treat others as we desire ourselves to be treated; that is a just maxim and very pleasing to God; and he who upholds that maxim shall be greatly blessed.

Und jeder von uns erzeige dem andern, was wir wollen, dass uns erzeigt werde; das ist ein gerechter und Gott höchst wohlgefälliger Grundsatz; und der wird höchst selig sein, wer solchen Grundsatz festhält.
And let each of us offer the other what we wish to be offered to us: that is a just principle and most pleasing to God; and he will be most blessed who keeps that principle.
div.note: Liebermann compares VI Atr 49.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
